summary:
This is an unofficial, deterministic approximation of the intraday index-futures model that TJR (@TJRTrades) teaches in his public 2025-2026 material, mainly Path to Profitability (Jan 2026) and 'My UPDATED Day Trading Strategy (2026)' (2026-06-05). It runs on ES and NQ on New York time with DST-safe bars. CME futures stand in for the charts he shows. His actual execution venue is unverified; it is probably index CFDs.

The model works in this order:
1. Mark external draws on liquidity: PDH/PDL of the 18:00-17:00 futures day, the Asia 18:00-03:00 high/low, the London 03:00-08:30 high/low, the pre-market high/low, the previous NY high/low, and unswept 1H/4H two-candle swings. NDOG/NWOG, the news candle and PWH/PWL are optional. Internal liquidity (unfilled HTF FVGs) is marked too, for targets only.
2. From 08:30 on, a level is traded through. A wick is enough.
3. 5m confirmation against the sweep is whichever comes first: a body close through the most recent 5m swing (BOS), or a body close through the floor/ceiling of the most recent FVG stack in the leg that ran into the level (IFVG).
4. A retrace, seen as a 1m BOS against the trade. By default it must reach 5m equilibrium or a 5m FVG of the new leg. TJR's 2026-06-05 simplification drops that zone requirement; both configurations come from him and both are reported.
5. A 1m BOS or 1m IFVG event back in trade direction is a market entry, only between 09:50 and 10:30 ET (10:30 is his personal cutoff), and only when ES and NQ 5m order flow agree. HTF bias (4H/1H swing sequence, HTF-gap respect, side of stacked draws) acts as a lean by default, not as a veto.
6. The stop sits beyond the retrace swing (the 'second high/low') plus a buffer of 2 ticks on ES, scaled up on NQ.
7. Targets are the next opposing external or internal draws, with TP1 >= 1R. At TP1, take a partial and move the stop to break-even; a runner continues.
8. Risk is 1% calculated per trade (our safety default; he now uses fixed contracts) and 1 trade per day (his beginner recommendation). FOMC, CPI and NFP days are skipped. On PPI and other red releases the bot waits 15-20 minutes and halves size.

Order and breaker blocks are excluded; he retired them as continuation confluences (stated 2026-02-03). The build is lookahead-free:
- every object carries anchor_t and detected_at
- FVGs are never deleted
- triggers are one-off events
- each setup locks its timeframe ladder
- history is built per contract
- fills follow an explicit order state machine

Where his statements conflict, the choices are exposed as parameters or variants. Independent mechanical replications did not reproduce his self-reported 64% daily win rate, and costs relative to his very tight stops dominate results. The trading bot, the signal notifier and the video monitor are labelled as unofficial and TJR-inspired. They speak in a neutral third-person voice and never speak or post as TJR.
instruments: ES (CME E-mini S&P 500 futures): primary. Serves as the data/execution proxy for his S&P charts and is always evaluated together with NQ.
MES / MNQ micros for small accounts: same rules, tick value 1.25 / 0.50 USD. Fees do not scale down by 1/10, so cost in R is roughly 2-4x higher.

Index CFDs (US500/NAS100 on MT5): probably his actual 2023-2025 execution venue (SPX500/Nas100 recap titles, AirFX/MT5 in Boot Camp 2.0, 'before fees and swap'). Available only as variant venue='cfd', with spread + swap costs and venue-dependent 4H alignment.
SPY / QQQ only as research proxies: they have no overnight session, so Asia/London levels are missing, and wicks depend on the feed.

Out of scope: gold, forex (GBPUSD, GBPJPY) and crypto. He teaches them too, but they have no ES/NQ SMT partner and use different sessions and news exposure. Each would need its own instrument table and session windows (e.g. GC tick 0.10 = 10 USD).
timezone: America/New_York (ET). DST-aware wall-clock binning is required; never use a fixed UTC offset, and never use pandas resample with an ET origin, which drifts by 1h during EDT. A futures trading day runs from 18:00 ET the previous day to the session end (17:00 ET or an early close), taken from an exchange calendar. 17:00-18:00 is the untradeable spread hour.

components.name: data_and_timeframes
components.description: Bar construction, timestamp convention, DST-safe resampling, contract roll, integer-tick arithmetic, warm-up, instrument table and the no-lookahead rules every other component relies on.
components.algorithm:
INPUT: 1m OHLCV per contract for ES and NQ (plus MES/MNQ if micros are allowed), UTC index. All wall-clock logic runs in America/New_York.
LOAD CHECKS: (1) Bar label convention: bar.t must be the interval START (Databento ohlcv ts_event). Assert that on CPI/NFP days the 08:30 ET spike sits in the bar labelled 08:30; otherwise shift labels by -1m. (2) Prices -> integer ticks: p = round(price/0.25); do every comparison in ints; round derived levels conservatively (equilibrium, extension_79, stop_loss). (3) Never forward-fill missing 1m bars. A bar missing on one index means 'no update' for that index, never a flat bar. ES and NQ timestamps must align. Days with more than max_missing_min missing minutes in [08:30, 12:00) on either index -> SKIP_DATA.
TIME CONVENTION (every swing, level, FVG, BOS, IFVG, sweep): anchor_t = open time of the bar where its price sits; detected_at = close_time of the bar that revealed it. An object is usable at decision time T iff detected_at <= T. Comparisons of the form 'inside the leg' or 'after X' use anchor_t.
BAR: bar.t = open; close_time = min(key + tf, session_end), with session_end from the exchange calendar (17:00 ET or the early close).
DST-SAFE RESAMPLING (1m -> 5m, 15m, 1H, 4H): wall = ts.tz_convert('America/New_York').tz_localize(None); anchor = (wall - 18h).normalize() + 18h; key = anchor + floor((wall - anchor)/tf)*tf. Do NOT use pandas resample(origin=18:00 ET) or offset='18h': during EDT the bins drift to 19/23/03/07/11/15 (verified with pandas 3.0.6). The recipe is exact because DST switches (Sunday 02:00) always fall inside the weekend closure. 4H bars open at 18, 22, 02, 06, 10, 14 (the last one is 3h). Assert for every day that a 4H bar closes at 10:00 ET.
TRADING DAY D = [18:00 ET of the previous session, session_end of D), taken from an exchange calendar (exchange_calendars 'CMES' or pandas_market_calendars 'CME_Equity'). A Globex-only holiday session is merged into the next trading day for PDH/PDL.
AVAILABILITY: at T (close of a 1m bar) a tf-bar is readable only if close_time <= T. A forming higher-TF candle is never read.
CONTRACT ROLL: roll ES, NQ, MES and MNQ together on the CME roll date (2nd Thursday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec = 8 calendar days before the 3rd-Friday expiry), from one explicit calendar. For trading day D, build EVERY historical object (levels, swings, FVGs, trend/orderflow state, warm-up) from the 1m history of the contract traded on D; that contract trades for months before the roll. Never splice raw prices. Panama back-adjustment (spread from the 16:00 ET prints of both contracts) is only a logged fallback when that history is missing. Unit test: no swing or FVG spans a contract change. Optional: skip the roll day.
WARM-UP: start all state machines at D - (lookback_4h_days + 10) trading days. Convergence test: decisions for D must be identical when the warm-up is doubled.
LADDERS: L_aligned = {confirm_tf 5m, trigger_tf 1m, tp_ref_tf 15m}. L_conflict (see daily_bias) = {confirm_tf 15m, trigger_tf 5m, tp_ref_tf 1H}. A setup locks its ladder at creation (S.ladder); ladder changes affect only new setups and are logged. Bar-count parameters (sweep_max_age, leg_max_bars, SMT windows) are counted in bars of S.ladder.confirm_tf and converted to time with that tf.
INSTRUMENT TABLE (verify against CME contract specs): tick 0.25 for ES, NQ, MES, MNQ. Tick value ES 12.50, NQ 5.00, MES 1.25, MNQ 0.50 USD. Point value ES 50, NQ 20, MES 5, MNQ 2. Commission + exchange + NFA fees per round trip: ES/NQ about 4.50, MES/MNQ about 1.00-1.50 (broker-specific).
VENUE: CME futures are the DATA PROXY for the charts he shows; his execution venue is unverified (probably index CFDs on MT5). venue='cfd' variant: cost = spread + overnight swap, and MT5 server 4H bars close at 09:00/13:00 ET, so the premise that the 4H candle closes at 10:00 depends on the venue.
Per-bar update order: see daily_orchestration.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.why: TJR sets charts to New York time. Fixed UTC offsets silently shift session ranges twice a year, a documented bug in third-party bots and in the MT5 thesis EA (ET_UTC_OffsetHours=-5).

parameters.name: four_hour_origin
parameters.why: Only an 18:00 origin makes a 4H candle close at 10:00, as he states in video 096 and as TradingView CME charts show. One third-party bot uses 17:00. The alignment is venue-dependent.

parameters.name: ladder_aligned
parameters.why: '5-minute order flow dictates everything ... then I scale down to the 1-minute to look for an entry'.

parameters.name: ladder_conflict
parameters.why: 2024 video 67vLAkcdPu4: if 4H and 1H disagree, demand 15m confirmation. Not restated in 2026.

parameters.name: max_missing_min
parameters.why: Our assumption; gaps in the 08:30-12:00 window corrupt sweeps and triggers.

parameters.name: venue
parameters.why: His venue is unverified. The CFD variant changes costs (spread + swap) and 4H bar alignment.

parameters.name: warmup_days
parameters.why: Trend, swing and FVG state depend on history; the convergence test checks that the warm-up is sufficient.

components.discretionary_notes: TJR reads charts visually and never specifies bar alignment. The 18:00 wall-clock 4H origin, the stop-first rule, integer ticks and per-contract history are our engineering choices. He rejects bar-replay backtests because the HTF candle is shown completed; the availability rule (detected_at <= T) is the code-level fix for exactly that lookahead.

components.name: sessions
components.description: Session windows (ET) used to build session high/low levels. Only the NY cash session is traded.
components.algorithm:
Windows are defined on bar OPEN time t: a 1m bar belongs to [a, b) iff a <= t < b.
For trading day D:
  ASIA   = [18:00 (evening before D), 03:00)
  LONDON = [london_start, 08:30)   # truncated when the next session opens
  NY_PRE = [08:30, 09:30)   # observe only, never enter
  NY_RTH = [09:30, ny_rth_end)
  SPREAD = [17:00, 18:00)   # no trading
For each session s: s.high/s.low = extremes of its 1m bars; formed_at (= detected_at) = s.end. A session level is usable at T only if formed_at <= T. With a london_end variant later than 08:30, the London H/L is neither trigger nor target before it forms.
london_start: london_anchor = 'fixed_ET_0300' (default, his ET session boxes) or 'london_local_0800' (= 04:00 ET in the weeks when US and UK DST dates differ). Log mismatch days.
PDH/PDL = extremes of the whole trading day D-1 [18:00, session_end). PREV_NY_H/L = extremes of NY_RTH of D-1.
Asia and London only mark levels; indexes are not traded there.

parameters.name: asia_window
parameters.range: start 18:00 | 19:00 | 20:00. 20:00-00:00 is the ICT Asian range used by third-party scripts, not TJR's.
parameters.why: Time Theory (L4xz2o23aPQ, 2026-01-12) and his newest liquidity guide use 18:00.

parameters.name: london_window
parameters.range: end 08:30 | 11:00 | 11:30 (later ends make London H/L unusable until formed)
parameters.why: He ends each session when the next one opens ('technically London goes till 11:30').

parameters.name: ny_pre_start
parameters.why: 08:30 for indexes; 08:00 is his forex / single-video variant.

parameters.name: ny_rth_end
parameters.why: 17:00 matches his NY session box (09:30-17:00). 16:00 is the cash-close variant, since 16:00-17:00 is not RTH.

parameters.name: london_anchor
parameters.why: He draws ET-fixed boxes. The local-time anchor is our test option for the DST-mismatch weeks.

components.discretionary_notes: His NY-session window for NY highs/lows conflicts between videos (09:30-17:00 vs 08:30-18:00), so we split it into NY_PRE and NY_RTH. The availability rule for later London ends is ours.

components.name: schedule
components.description: Intraday clock: manipulation window, entry window, alignment deadline, cutoff and time exits.
components.algorithm:
Decisions are made at 1m closes T (ET).
T < 09:30: never enter. Sweeps and confirmations are tracked from scan_start (bars with t >= 08:30).
[09:30, entry_start): the 'manipulation' window, where the sweep is expected. A trigger event with T < entry_start is ignored and logged as PRE_WINDOW_TRIGGER. The setup stays ARMED and needs a NEW trigger event with T >= entry_start; it is never cancelled just for being early.
entries_allowed(T) = entry_start <= T < cutoff AND day is not NO_TRADE AND no news block at T (filters) AND trades_today < max_trades_per_day AND day is not DONE.
[09:50, 10:10): preferred 'macro' window (4H/1H close at 10:00). Log in_macro; prefer_macro_only restricts entries to this window.
ALIGNMENT DEADLINE (mode 'orderflow', default): at the first 1m close T >= alignment_deadline, the day is DONE if orderflow[ES][5m] != orderflow[NQ][5m] or either is NONE. Otherwise continue until cutoff with setups in any state. Mode 'strict' (variant): DONE if no CONFIRMED/ARMED setup has a direction equal to the common orderflow.
T >= cutoff: cancel all un-entered setups; no new setups. Open positions are NOT closed at cutoff.
Time exits for an open position, whichever comes first: stall_exit and max_hold_minutes (trade_management), pre-event flatten (filters), flat_time = min(15:55, session_end - 5 min). The bot never holds overnight or over a weekend (our rule).
PM session disabled by default ('Me, personally, I don't trade this').

parameters.name: entry_start
parameters.why: 'from 9:50 to 10:10 we have our entry period'; 'at 9:41 I typically don't take trades'. The edge is soft ('sometimes 9:45').

parameters.name: cutoff
parameters.why: This is his personal preference, not a rule of the setup: 'If I can't find a trade by 10:30, I'm done for the day' (2026-01-12, 2026-05-07, 2026-06-05). The same 2026-06-05 video calls an 11:05-11:20 entry 'technically when you would want to enter using our strategy', though he skips it.

parameters.name: prefer_macro_only
parameters.why: 09:50-10:10 is a preference, not a hard rule ('I take trades at 10:20 sometimes').

parameters.name: alignment_deadline
parameters.why: 'If neither of the indexes are aligned and it's 10:20 ... call it a day'. This refers to ES/NQ 5m order-flow agreement, not to setup state.

parameters.name: alignment_deadline_mode
parameters.why: The orderflow mode follows the quote. The strict mode is our stricter reading.

parameters.name: flat_time
parameters.why: Our assumption. Whether he is always flat by the close is unverified: his 2026 account figures are quoted 'before fees and swap'.

parameters.name: max_hold_minutes
parameters.why: Our backstop, from 'I like to catch one to three-hour moves'. The progress-based stall_exit handles stalled trades first.

components.discretionary_notes: All his time edges are soft, and he has traded later (10:45, around 12:00, PM). A third-party bot missed 31 of his recap trades because of a hard 10:30 cutoff, yet loosening it worsened P&L. Keep 10:30 as the default and test 11:00, 11:30 and none as TJR-sourced variants. flat_time, max_hold and the no-overnight rule are ours.

components.name: key_levels
components.description: External draws on liquidity marked before the open on BOTH ES and NQ, which act as sweep triggers and targets. Internal liquidity (imbalances) is marked as targets and bias draws only.
components.algorithm:
Per index X, built from the contract traded on D. Level = {id, type, side HIGH|LOW, price_ticks, tf_rank, anchor_t, formed_at, alive, cluster_id, resistance}.
At scan_start (08:30) of day D build:
  PDH/PDL (trading day D-1)                               rank 3
  ASIA_H/L (formed 03:00), LONDON_H/L (formed 08:30)       rank 2
  PREV_NY_H/L (if include_prev_ny)                         rank 2
  1H two-candle swing H/L with detected_at <= 08:30 from the last lookback_1h_days    rank 3
  4H two-candle swing H/L from the last lookback_4h_days                               rank 4
  optional: PWH/PWL (include_weekly; week = Sun 18:00 -> Fri session_end) rank 5; daily two-candle swing H/L (htf_stack includes D) rank 5; NEWS_H/L = high/low of the 1m bar of a red USD release today (include_news_candle), formed at that bar's close
ALIVE: a HIGH level dies at the first 1m bar after formed_at with high > price (LOW: low < price).
CANDIDATES at 08:30 = alive levels with formed_at <= 08:30. A level already pushed through in Asia/London is dead ('there was no reaction off of it ... that draw on liquidity is pretty much useless').
LATE JOINERS: PRE_H/L = extremes of [08:30, 09:30), formed at 09:30 (include_premarket). 1H/4H swings detected after 08:30 join at their detected_at.
DEDUPE: identical (index, side, price_ticks) -> one level. Keep the highest tf_rank and the earliest formed_at, and take the union of types.
CLUSTERS: same-side levels within eq_tol = max(2 ticks, ceil(eq_tol_pct*price/tick)) form a cluster; strength = count (relatively equal highs/lows = stronger draw). Each level is still swept individually.
RESISTANCE (used only when draw_weighting = 'resistance'): LOW-resistance if the level is in a cluster (strength >= 2) or part of an LRL run (>= 3 consecutive same-side 5m/15m swings of today that step monotonically toward price, e.g. rising lows under price); otherwise HIGH-resistance. LOW-resistance draws weigh 2 in bias draw counts and win TP ties.
INTERNAL LIQUIDITY (targets and bias draws only, never sweep triggers): eligible unfilled FVGs on tp_ref_tf and higher (15m/1H/4H). If include_opening_gaps: NDOG = gap between the last close before 17:00 and the 18:00 open, formed daily at 18:00; NWOG = gap between the Friday close and the Sunday 18:00 open; each is alive until fully traded through. NCOG is ignored.
A swept level is never reused as a trigger or target on the same day.

parameters.name: lookback_1h_days
parameters.why: Our assumption; TJR gives no lookback.

parameters.name: lookback_4h_days
parameters.why: Our assumption (a third-party 'OURS' value).

parameters.name: include_prev_ny
parameters.why: He lists 'New York highs, New York lows' among session draws.

parameters.name: include_premarket
parameters.why: In a third-party replay, omitting NY/pre-market levels caused most 'no level pushed through' stand-downs.

parameters.name: include_news_candle
parameters.why: Off for simplicity, not because of his teaching. On 2026-01-05 he calls news-candle H/L 'very very beneficial ... high probability draws in liquidity', so test true.

parameters.name: include_weekly
parameters.why: PWH/PWL belong to the older D/W top-down layer; optional.

parameters.name: include_opening_gaps
parameters.why: NDOG/NWOG are defined in Advanced Imbalance Concepts (2026-01-08). He prefers NWOG but admits he rarely uses them.

parameters.name: eq_tol_pct
parameters.why: His only example: two S&P lows 'literally 50 cents apart' are close enough (about 0.5 pt on ES).

parameters.name: draw_weighting
parameters.why: Relative-equal highs/lows attract 'four times the amount of buy orders' (2026-01-05). The weighting numbers are ours.

parameters.name: scan_start
parameters.why: A pre-market sweep can be the day's sweep.

components.discretionary_notes: He marks 'all of them' and, asked which one price will target, says 'you don't need to know'. The following are our deterministic choices: lookbacks, tolerance, the dead-level rule for pre-08:30 breaches, treating NDOG/NWOG as internal (target-only) liquidity, and the LRL/resistance proxy. BPR (overlap of opposing FVGs) is mentioned in his 2026 tutorial but left as an off-by-default variant.

components.name: swing_detection
components.description: TJR's two-candle swing high/low definition, run separately on every timeframe.
components.algorithm:
prev = None
for i, b in enumerate(bars):            # completed bars of ONE timeframe, one contract, integer ticks
    if b.close == b.open: continue      # doji skipped (our handling)
    if prev is not None:
        p = bars[prev]
        if p.close > p.open and b.close < b.open:     # up candle then down candle
            emit SwingHigh(price = max(high[prev..i]), anchor_t = t of the argmax bar, detected_at = b.close_time)
        elif p.close < p.open and b.close > b.open:   # down candle then up candle
            emit SwingLow(price = min(low[prev..i]), anchor_t = t of the argmin bar, detected_at = b.close_time)
    prev = i
Two same-colour candles never form a swing. No N-bar lookback, no size/ATR filter. 'Most recent swing' = the latest one with detected_at <= T, even a lower low inside an uptrend.

parameters.name: swing_mode
parameters.why: 'A high consists of an up candle, then a down candle ... the highest wick of those two'. Fractal pivots sit 35-44% farther from price, which roughly doubles stops.

parameters.name: doji_rule
parameters.why: Our assumption (a third-party TJR indicator ignores dojis).

components.discretionary_notes: He sometimes speaks of 'significant' highs/lows chosen by eye; the two-candle rule is his stated definition and is what we code. Third-party interpretation, not TJR: https://in.tradingview.com/scripts/candlestick/page-2/

components.name: structure_break
components.description: Close-based break of structure, a shared order-flow state (BOS + IFVG), and the HTF trend rule including a range/consolidation state.
components.algorithm:
Per (index, tf): sh/sl = most recent swing high/low (each with a broken flag); state is read as of the bar's open.
on each completed bar b:
    if sl and not sl.broken and b.close < sl.price:  sl.broken = True; emit BOS{dir: DOWN, ref: sl, detected_at: b.close_time}
    if sh and not sh.broken and b.close > sh.price:  sh.broken = True; emit BOS{dir: UP, ref: sh, detected_at: b.close_time}
    then register swings detected at b.close_time (the newest replaces sh/sl)
Rules: body close only (wicks never count); close == level is not a break; only the newest swing is watched; no displacement/body-size requirement. A TJR reversal 'BOS' = the first close through the most recent opposite swing (standard SMC calls this CHoCH/MSS).
TREND (5m, 1m, and 4H/1H when htf_trend_rule = 'single_break'): trend = direction of the latest BOS (NONE before the first).
ORDERFLOW[X][tf] in {UP, DOWN, NONE} = direction of the latest BOS event OR stack-level IFVG event on that (index, tf). A bearish IFVG sets DOWN and a bullish one sets UP. It is stamped with detected_at. index_alignment, the alignment deadline, the lean bias check and the chop proxy all use it.
HTF TREND (4H/1H, htf_trend_rule = 'hh_hl_sequence', default): keep the last two confirmed swing highs (SH1 older, SH2) and lows (SL1, SL2). UP iff the latest BOS on tf was UP AND SH2 > SH1 AND SL2 > SL1. DOWN iff the latest BOS was DOWN AND SH2 < SH1 AND SL2 < SL1. Otherwise RANGE (consolidation), which counts as NONE for bias. A lower low that sweeps a low changes nothing until a close-based BOS.

parameters.name: bos_requires_close
parameters.why: 'It's not a candlestick wick. It's a candlestick closure'.

parameters.name: impulse_body_min
parameters.why: Body > 50% of range is a third-party filter (TJR v4, ds82385), not TJR's rule.

parameters.name: htf_trend_rule
parameters.why: His daily-bias lesson (ironJFzNBic, 2026-01-14) defines 4H/1H trends as HH+HL / LH+LL sequences. Day 44 warns that 'a 5m BOS is often just a 15m retracement'. single_break was the draft behaviour; test both.

components.discretionary_notes: Conflict: the draft's single-break HTF trend vs his HH/HL sequence definition; both are exposed. Consolidation ('uptrend, downtrend, consolidation', Order Flow Explained 2025-02-20) is modelled as RANGE. Adding IFVG to the order-flow state is our reading of 'either via break of structure or an inverse fair value gap'. Third-party interpretations, not TJR: https://videohighlight.com/v/PmhuPbY8ZHo?mediaType=youtube&language=en&summaryType=compressed&summaryId=lpgf26EeRjKnZmzR26eJ&aiFormatted=false, https://quizlet.com/810912109/tjr-strategy-flash-cards/, https://www.tradingview.com/script/N3UmFTLJ-TJR-BOS-CHOCH-Real-time-Swings/

components.name: fvg
components.description: Fair value gap detection, a never-delete lifecycle with snapshot eligibility, stacking, and stack-level IFVG events.
components.algorithm:
DETECT at completed bar i >= 2 of a tf: c1 = bars[i-2], c2 = bars[i-1], c3 = bars[i]. All three must be time-contiguous (c3.t - c1.t == 2*tf) and lie in one trading day and one contract.
  bullish if c3.low - c1.high >= min_fvg_ticks: zone [bottom = c1.high, top = c3.low]
  bearish if c1.low - c3.high >= min_fvg_ticks: zone [bottom = c3.high, top = c1.low]
  record G = {id, index, tf, dir, bottom, top, c1_t, anchor_t = c2.t, detected_at = c3.close_time, touched_at: None, inverted_at: None, expired_at: None, stack_id}. Candle colours are irrelevant; overlapping wicks = no gap. Gaps are NEVER deleted.
ELIGIBILITY for any consumer evaluating bar b (snapshot as of b's open): eligible(G, b) = G.detected_at <= b.t AND (G.inverted_at is None OR G.inverted_at >= b.close_time) AND (G.expired_at is None OR G.expired_at > b.t). A gap inverted by b itself therefore still counts for b.
LIFECYCLE on later bars j:
  touched_at = first j with (bullish) low <= top / (bearish) high >= bottom. This is a fill, not an invalidation.
  inverted_at = j.close_time of the first j with (bullish) close < bottom / (bearish) close > top (body close). A single gap inverting emits NO event.
  expired_at: (a) the gap is untouched and a 1m wick trades beyond the first same-direction swing with anchor_t > G.anchor_t (usable only after that swing's detected_at) ('once we push above the high ... we no longer need these gaps'), or (b) age > fvg_max_age[tf].
  Gaps are never dragged forward in time.
STACKS (our rule): same-direction gaps whose middle candles are separated only by candles of the same colour (dojis allowed) share one stack_id. For a caller with leg start t0: bullish floor = min(bottom) over members with c1_t >= t0 (inverted members included); bearish ceiling = max(top).
STACK IFVG EVENT: when a bar closes below the floor of a bullish stack (bearish IFVG) or above the ceiling of a bearish stack (bullish IFVG), emit IFVG{stack_id, dir, index, tf, detected_at}. Only this stack-level event counts as an IFVG ('the last fair value gap that is holding up the trend'). For the global orderflow state, the stack is the one containing the most recently detected eligible gap, with t0 = none.
UNIT TEST: in a synthetic 5-bar series where bar 5 closes through a bullish gap, confirmation must return confirm_kind == 'IFVG' at bar 5.

parameters.name: min_fvg_ticks
parameters.why: TJR states no minimum and uses 'the tiniest bullish gap ever created'.

parameters.name: fvg_max_age
parameters.default: 1m: 2h; 5m: 24h; 15m: 3 trading days; 1H: 10 trading days; 4H: 20 trading days
parameters.why: Our assumption. Ages are set per timeframe in time units; a single bar count would mean 4.8h on 1m but 48 days on 4H.

parameters.name: stack_rule
parameters.why: Our deterministic reading of 'no retrace between gaps'.

components.discretionary_notes: Expiry, stack grouping and the snapshot/never-delete lifecycle are ours; he points at 'the' gap on the chart. The never-delete rule fixes a real bug: if an inverted gap is removed from 'alive' before consumers run, IFVG confirmations and the HTF-gap bias flip can never fire. Third-party interpretation, not TJR: https://quizlet.com/810912109/tjr-strategy-flash-cards/

components.name: ifvg
components.description: Inverse FVG: a body close through an opposite-direction FVG stack, used as confirmation (5m) and as trigger (1m).
components.algorithm:
Bearish IFVG at bar b w.r.t. bullish stack K: b.close < K.floor(t0) (strict). Bullish IFVG w.r.t. bearish stack K: b.close > K.ceiling(t0).
Stack selection (ifvg_stack_rule), using only gaps eligible for b:
  'most_recent_stack_floor' (default, matches his examples): K = the stack containing the most recently detected eligible opposite-direction gap with c1_t >= t0.
  'deepest_in_leg': the floor is min(bottom) over all eligible opposite gaps with c1_t >= t0.
t0 by caller: step 2 (confirmation) uses S.leg_origin_t, the leg that ran into the swept level (see liquidity_sweep). Step 4 (trigger) uses S.range_low_bar.t (LONG: range_high_bar.t), the retrace leg.
Evaluated only inside a setup with a registered sweep; never a standalone entry ('can't just be taking sell positions on inverse fair value gaps willy-nilly'). IFVG and BOS are interchangeable; whichever prints first counts. Each stack can fire at most once per setup.

parameters.name: ifvg_enabled
parameters.why: 'I use this confluence almost every single day, almost more than break of structure'. It fires earlier and gives a tighter stop.

parameters.name: ifvg_stack_rule
parameters.why: One rule must be chosen; the two differ whenever a leg holds more than one stack. The default matches his chart examples.

components.discretionary_notes: Which stack in the leg counts is our rule. In a third-party test the IFVG shrank stops by only 10-15% (not the ~2x he describes) and only helped when the inversion was fresh. Third-party transcript site (unverified, blocked from research): https://sozai.app/transcript/path-to-profitability-tjr-strategy/

components.name: equilibrium
components.description: 50% of the most recent swing range of the new order flow. A continuation (pullback) zone, never an entry by itself.
components.algorithm:
SHORT setup after step-2 confirmation (LONG mirrors):
  range_high = the latest confirm_tf swing high with anchor_t in [S.sweep_extreme_bar.t, S.range_low_bar.t) and detected_at <= T; if none, S.sweep_extreme
  range_low  = S.range_low (lowest low since the sweep-extreme bar, extended on every new low)
  EQ in integer ticks: SHORT touch level = ceil((range_high + range_low)/2); LONG touch level = floor(...). A touch must reach the true midpoint.
  premium = price >= EQ (sell only from premium); LONG: discount = price <= EQ.
  Re-anchor on every new range extreme. Once touched, EQ is frozen until a new extreme prints, which also resets the retrace flags.
  Touch: SHORT if a 1m high >= EQ; LONG if a 1m low <= EQ (a wick poke counts, no close needed).
  entry_premium_check (enforced at the entry gate): 'none' (default) | 'trigger_close_in_premium' (SHORT trigger close >= EQ) | 'retrace_high_in_premium' (equivalent to the touch).

parameters.name: eq_anchor
parameters.why: 'from the most recent swing low up to the most recent swing high'. Anchoring to older swings is the #1 student error he names. The impulse-candle midpoint is an older third-party reading.

parameters.name: entry_premium_check
parameters.why: He says to sell from premium but never states which price must be in premium; the touch already covers the retrace.

components.discretionary_notes: Tick rounding and the premium check are ours. Third-party interpretation, not TJR: https://quizlet.com/810912109/tjr-strategy-flash-cards/

components.name: extension_79
components.description: Optional '79% extension closure' confirmation, disabled by default. He says he rarely uses it, and it is absent from the 2026 re-teachings.
components.algorithm:
SHORT: A = S.leg_origin price, B = S.sweep_extreme; lvl79 = floor_ticks(B - 0.79*(B - A)). Confirmation if a completed confirm_tf bar (step 2) or trigger_tf bar (step 4) closes < lvl79.
LONG: A = leg-origin high, B = sweep low; lvl79 = ceil_ticks(B + 0.79*(A - B)); confirm if close > lvl79.
Never used as a stop or target.

parameters.name: enable_ext79
parameters.why: 'I rarely use this one, you guys can very well do without this'.

components.discretionary_notes: The anchoring (79% of the way back from the leg extreme toward its origin) is inferred from on-screen use and matches the MT5 thesis EA; he never states it as a formula.

components.name: smt
components.description: ES vs NQ divergence at a swept draw. Evaluated once at a fixed time and then frozen. It strengthens bias and can select the index; it is not a trigger by itself (info-only by default).
components.algorithm:
When setup S (index X, dir) registers its first sweep of level L at t_s = sweep detected_at: Y = the other index, tf = S.ladder.confirm_tf.
t_eval = close of the smt_after_bars-th tf bar closing after t_s (default: the first). SMT is unavailable before t_eval, is evaluated exactly once at t_eval, and is then FROZEN; a later Y sweep never unsets it. It never references confirm_time.
Window W = [t_s - smt_window_bars*tf, t_eval].
ref_X = L.price. ref_Y = Y's level of the same type (Y.LONDON_H for X.LONDON_H, Y.PDH for X.PDH, ...). If there is none (1H/4H swing): ref_Y = max(Y.high) over Y bars with anchor within +-smt_align_bars*tf of L.anchor_t (LONG: min low).
Bearish SMT (SHORT): max(X.high in W) > ref_X AND max(Y.high in W) <= ref_Y. Bullish (LONG): min(X.low in W) < ref_X AND min(Y.low in W) >= ref_Y.
leading_index = Y (the one that failed to make the new extreme, 'already more bearish'); lagging_index = X.
SMT completion target: the leg-origin low (bearish) / high (bullish) of the diverging swing.
smt_mode: 'info' (default, log only) | 'select_leading' | 'select_lagging' (trade only that index; needs cross_index_sweep when it is not the sweeping index) | 'required' | 'confirmation' (counts as a step-2 confirmation with confirmation time t_eval). Ignored when the sweep is not at a marked draw.

parameters.name: smt_mode
parameters.why: 'It doesn't tell me to take a trade ... it just helps strengthen my bias'. The UPDATED-2026 video trades whichever index produced the sweep.

parameters.name: smt_after_bars
parameters.why: Our assumption. A fixed evaluation time keeps the test monotonic and lookahead-free.

parameters.name: smt_window_bars
parameters.why: Our assumption; his swings must be simultaneous.

parameters.name: smt_align_bars
parameters.why: Our assumption for 'same bar' pairing.

components.discretionary_notes: Leading vs lagging is UNRESOLVED as of 2026. In 2025 he says to trade the leading index. The newest SMT video (FJch02ucIO8, 2026-01-27) frames NASDAQ as 'the lagging index ... is going to eventually follow suit', and one extraction reads that as trading the lagging index. The 2026-06-05 video simply trades the index that produced the sweep. 'Leading' is never formally defined. SMT only works for the ES/NQ pair.

components.name: daily_bias
components.description: HTF bias from the 4H/1H swing sequence, HTF-FVG respect/disrespect and the side of stacked draws. By default it is a LEAN (TJR 2026), not a veto.
components.algorithm:
Computed at 09:25 ET and at every completed 1H bar until cutoff (bias may flip intraday). Results apply to new setups; S.ladder stays locked.
for X in (ES, NQ), tf in htf_stack (default 4H, 1H):
    tr = HTF trend per structure_break.htf_trend_rule (RANGE -> NONE)
    K = the most recent FVG stack in direction tr detected after the BOS that set tr, whether or not it is still alive
    if K has a stack-level IFVG event against tr with detected_at <= T: tr = opposite(tr)   # 'we disrespect this gap ... no longer bearish'
    trend[X][tf] = tr
Index combination (our assumption): t_tf = trend[ES][tf] if it equals trend[NQ][tf], else NONE.
if t4 != NONE and t1 == t4: bias = t4; ladder = L_aligned
elif t4 != NONE and t1 != NONE: bias = t4; ladder = L_conflict (2024 rule; NO_TRADE if htf_conflict_action == 'stand_down')
elif exactly one of t4, t1 != NONE: bias = that one; ladder = L_aligned
else: bias = NEUTRAL
htf_stack 'D+4H+1H' (2023 Boot Camp variant): daily bars run 18:00-session_end and use the same swing/structure logic. If trend[D] is set and differs from t4 on both indexes -> NO_TRADE (variant: 0.5x risk).
DRAWS: for each index X, up_X / dn_X = weighted count (key_levels.draw_weighting) of usable alive key levels and internal-liquidity zones above/below X's own last 1m close within draw_radius_pct. Bias UP survives only if up_ES > 0 AND up_NQ > 0, else NEUTRAL (DOWN mirrors). If NEUTRAL and |(up_ES + up_NQ) - (dn_ES + dn_NQ)| >= draw_imbalance_min, bias = the side with more draws. Record which levels were counted as bias-side draws.
PHASE: if htf_phase.phase_mode == 'lean', a RETRACEMENT phase makes the counter-trend direction count as with-bias until its internal zone is touched.
FILTER at trigger time (bias_eval = 'trigger' default | 'creation'):
  'lean' (default, TJR 2026): with-bias or NEUTRAL -> allowed. Counter-bias is allowed iff (a) at least one level counted as a bias-side draw in the latest computation is among S.levels (the draw the bias pointed to has been delivered), (b) SMT was detected at the sweep (if lean_requires_smt), and (c) the other index Y has an orderflow event (BOS or IFVG) on S.ladder.confirm_tf in trade direction with detected_at in [S.sweep_time, T].
  'filter' (third-party optimisation): SHORT iff bias in {DOWN, NEUTRAL}; LONG iff bias in {UP, NEUTRAL}.
  'off': no filter.
A bias failure keeps S ARMED (bias may flip at the 10:00 1H close) and requires a fresh trigger.

parameters.name: bias_mode
parameters.why: The 2026-06-05 strategy video never mentions a bias step. In the 2026-01-17 capstone he trades against his stated bias ('The market proved me wrong ... we can still make money'), and the 2026-01-14 lesson makes bias revisable. 'filter' raised net from -$4,222 to -$190 in a third-party replay; that is optimisation, not fidelity.

parameters.name: lean_requires_smt
parameters.why: The 2026-01-17 capstone's counter-bias trade came with SMT at the swept bias-side draw.

parameters.name: bias_eval
parameters.why: Bias can flip intraday; state explicitly which snapshot is used.

parameters.name: htf_stack
parameters.why: His 2026 material uses 4H as the top timeframe; the 2023 Boot Camp does a monthly/weekly/daily/4H top-down (Day 44: daily, 4H and 1H disagree -> no trade).

parameters.name: htf_conflict_action
parameters.why: 2024 rule from video 67vLAkcdPu4 (4H vs 1H conflict -> 15m confirmation), not restated in 2026. The Boot Camp stood down instead.

parameters.name: draw_radius_pct
parameters.why: Our assumption: draws within about 1% of price are reachable intraday.

parameters.name: draw_imbalance_min
parameters.why: Our assumption for 'the side where unswept draws are stacked'.

components.discretionary_notes: He gives no rule for combining trend, draws, HTF gaps and SMT. He says his 9:00 bias is often wrong and lets 5m order flow overrule it. Several rules are ours: requiring ES and NQ to agree on the 4H/1H trend, which HTF close flips bias, which gap 'holds the trend', and the draw counting. The HTF-gap flip was the only bias change that improved P&L in a third-party replay.

components.name: htf_phase
components.description: Optional 4H phase state (extension / retracement / continuation / reversal) and the external -> internal -> external liquidity cycle as a bias input. Off by default; measure its marginal effect.
components.algorithm:
Per index on 4H, phase_mode = 'off' (default) | 'log' | 'lean':
  EXTENSION: after a 4H close beyond the last external 4H swing in the trend direction.
  RETRACEMENT: after a 1H BOS against the 4H trend while the nearest eligible untouched 4H FVG (or the 4H EQ of the last 4H swing range) on the pullback side is untouched. The intraday draw is that internal zone (counter-trend lean).
  CONTINUATION: after that zone is touched and a 1H BOS prints in the 4H trend direction. The draw is the next external level in the trend direction.
  REVERSAL: the daily_bias HTF-gap disrespect flip.
'lean': in RETRACEMENT the counter-trend direction counts as with-bias for the lean filter until the zone is touched. 'log': record the phase only.

parameters.name: phase_mode
parameters.why: The concept is his: 'price is always either looking to take out external liquidity, which is highs and lows, or fill imbalances, which is internal liquidity' (Advanced Liquidity Concepts, 2026-01-05), and the 2026 tutorial's bias step 1 asks 'which phase are we in?'. The thresholds are ours, so it is off until tested.

components.discretionary_notes: He judges the phase by eye; the state transitions here are our deterministic proxy.

components.name: liquidity_sweep
components.description: Detects a key level being traded through and opens a setup. The sweep is only an opportunity until the step-2 confirmation.
components.algorithm:
Active for 1m bars with t >= scan_start and close_time < cutoff. Iterate ES then NQ, and levels sorted by (side, price_ticks), for determinism.
for X in (ES, NQ): for L in usable alive levels of X (formed_at <= bar.t):
    HIGH: if bar.high > L.price: L.alive = False; on_sweep(X, L, SHORT, bar)
    LOW:  if bar.low  < L.price: L.alive = False; on_sweep(X, L, LONG, bar)
(no close-back-inside requirement unless require_close_back_inside)
on_sweep(X, L, dir, bar):
    if X has a setup in dir with state SWEPT: append L to it; return      # stacked levels in one push
    if X has a setup in dir with state CONFIRMED/ARMED: log; return
    create S{id, index: X, dir, levels: [L], ladder: current ladder (locked), created_at = sweep_time = bar.close_time, sweep_anchor_t = bar.t,
             sweep_extreme = bar.high (SHORT) / bar.low (LONG), sweep_extreme_bar = bar, state: SWEPT}
    LEG ORIGIN (SHORT; LONG mirrors): t0 = anchor_t of the most recent confirm_tf swing high with price >= L.price and detected_at <= S.sweep_time (the last time price was at the level), floored at S.sweep_anchor_t - leg_max_bars*confirm_tf. S.leg_origin = min 1m low in [t0, sweep bar]; S.leg_origin_t = start of the confirm_tf bar containing that low.
while SWEPT: SHORT sweep_extreme = max(sweep_extreme, bar.high) (LONG: min low); sweep_extreme_bar follows the extreme.
EXPIRY: SWEPT for longer than sweep_max_age -> EXPIRED_NO_REACTION ('takes out a low and keeps going ... is it a liquidity sweep? No').
PRE-MARKET: premarket_sweep_policy 'accept_if_reacted' (default): a sweep in [08:30, 09:30) whose confirmation printed before 09:30 continues after the open. 'require_fresh': such setups are dropped at 09:30, today's 5m and 15m two-candle swings of [08:30, 09:30) are added as levels, and only sweeps at/after 09:30 count. premarket_unconfirmed: 'keep' (default, subject to sweep_max_age) | 'drop' for pre-market sweeps still SWEPT at 09:30.

parameters.name: require_close_back_inside
parameters.why: TJR: a wick through is enough; validation comes from the later 5m BOS/IFVG. Most third-party scripts require the reclaim.

parameters.name: sweep_max_age
parameters.default: 12 confirm_tf bars (60 min on 5m, 180 min on the 15m conflict ladder)
parameters.why: Our assumption (a third-party 'OURS' value).

parameters.name: leg_max_bars
parameters.why: Our cap on the leg into the level, used for IFVG stack selection and extension_79.

parameters.name: premarket_sweep_policy
parameters.why: Newest statement: 'if liquidity has already been swept during pre-market and we're already reacting off of it ... this was the liquidity sweep for the day'. Oct/Nov 2025 'step 2B' required a new 5m manipulation.

parameters.name: premarket_unconfirmed
parameters.why: Our rule for the case the policy above leaves open.

parameters.name: cross_index_sweep
parameters.why: 'As long as one of the indexes is doing it for us'. If true, the non-sweeping index may open a setup at the other's sweep time with its own local extreme.

components.discretionary_notes: Leg-origin rule, expiry and pre-market edge cases are ours. Third-party / unverified, not TJR sources: https://www.scribd.com/document/746481404/SMC-by-Tjrtrades-TJR-Ebook-En-es (e-book of unknown provenance, possibly paid material), https://sozai.app/transcript/teaching-friend-day-trade/

components.name: confirmation
components.description: Step 2: change of order flow on confirm_tf (5m) against the sweep, by BOS or IFVG, whichever comes first.
components.algorithm:
When a confirm_tf bar c of S.ladder closes, for each setup S with state SWEPT and c.close_time > S.sweep_time (SHORT; LONG mirrors), reading state as of c's open:
  msl  = most recent confirm_tf swing low with detected_at <= c.t and not broken (it may have formed after the sweep)
  bos  = msl is not None and c.close < msl.price
  K    = bullish confirm_tf stack per ifvg with t0 = S.leg_origin_t, using gaps eligible for c
  ifvg = K is not None and c.close < K.floor
  ext  = enable_ext79 and c.close < lvl79
  smt  = smt_mode == 'confirmation' and S.smt_bearish and S.smt_t_eval <= c.close_time
  if bos or ifvg or ext or smt:
      S.state = CONFIRMED; S.confirm_kind = first true of (ifvg, bos, ext, smt); S.confirm_time = c.close_time
      S.range_low = min 1m low from S.sweep_extreme_bar through c; S.range_low_bar = its bar
      S.zone_touched = S.counter_bos = False
Never enter on the confirmation bar ('As much as I would love to just enter straight off of that break of structure, I'm going to be patient').

parameters.name: confirmation_menu
parameters.why: 2026 teaching: 'either via break of structure or an inverse fair value gap'. The Nov 2025 menu also listed 79% and SMT.

components.discretionary_notes: Third-party / unverified summaries, not TJR sources: https://sozai.app/transcript/path-to-profitability-tjr-strategy/, https://www.studocu.com/in/document/mit-school-of-distance-education/foundations-of-business-management-hr-marketing-finance-operations/tjr-trading-strategy-key-levels-session-timing-guide/144532962

components.name: continuation
components.description: Step 3: wait for the retrace, seen on the 1m as a BOS against the trade. By default it must also reach 5m equilibrium or a 5m FVG of the new leg. TJR's own sources conflict on whether the zone is required.
components.algorithm:
For each 1m bar b after S.confirm_time while S.state in {CONFIRMED, ARMED} (SHORT; LONG mirrors).
PER-BAR ORDER: (1) entry trigger check on the PRE-BAR state (see entry), (2) cancel checks, (3) new-leg update, (4) zone / counter-BOS updates.
(2) CANCEL: b.high > S.sweep_extreme (hard); or a confirm_tf bar closes > S.range_high (cancel_ref = 'range_high', default: the retrace fully reclaimed the premium leg); or T >= cutoff. Variant cancel_ref = 'latest_swing_high_frozen_at_confirmation'.
(3) NEW LEG: if b.low < S.range_low and no entry happened on b: S.range_low = b.low; S.range_low_bar = b; S.state = CONFIRMED; zone_touched = counter_bos = False; unfreeze EQ.
(4) EQ per equilibrium; cont_gaps = bearish confirm_tf FVGs eligible for b with anchor_t >= S.sweep_extreme_bar.t
    if 'EQ' in continuation_zones and b.high >= EQ: zone_touched = True
    if 'FVG' in continuation_zones and any(b.high >= g.bottom for g in cont_gaps): zone_touched = True
    sh1 = most recent trigger_tf swing high with detected_at <= b.t and not broken; if b.t > S.range_low_bar.t and b is a completed trigger_tf bar with close > sh1.price: counter_bos = True; S.counter_bos_time = b.close_time   # 'I classify five-minute retraces as a break of structure to the upside on the one minute'
    S.retrace_high = max trigger_tf high after S.range_low_bar   # the 'second high'
    if counter_bos and (zone_touched or not require_zone_touch): S.state = ARMED; S.arm_time = b.close_time
If weekly strict_mode is enabled (off by default), the zone must be an FVG lying in premium (FVG AND EQ).
If price never retraces, the setup dies at cutoff (no chasing).

parameters.name: continuation_zones
parameters.why: 'The only continuation confluences that I need ... are equilibrium and fair value gaps'. Order and breaker blocks were retired as continuation confluences (stated 2026-02-03).

parameters.name: require_zone_touch
parameters.why: Documented TJR-internal conflict. Path to Profitability / the Jan 2026 capstone require the EQ/FVG step. The 2026-06-05 video says 'we can even make this even simpler ... we can just say we want a one minute break of structure' and 'you guys can use either'. Run and report both. Third-party partition tests found the zone filter did not improve entries.

parameters.name: cancel_ref
parameters.why: With two-candle swings, a normal retrace into EQ often closes above a minor lower high. Cancelling on that kills exactly the pullbacks the setup waits for. Measure how many setups each rule cancels.

components.discretionary_notes: The reset on new leg extremes, the cancel rules and the per-bar order are our deterministic reading of 'we need to see some form of a retrace'. Third-party summary, not a TJR source: https://coconote.app/notes/12bb34cc-95bf-4878-a877-852abf81eb56

components.name: entry
components.description: Step 4: a 1m BOS or 1m IFVG event back in trade direction after the armed retrace. Signal at the trigger close; the fill comes via backtest_execution / live_execution.
components.algorithm:
While S.state == ARMED, on each completed trigger_tf bar b, using the PRE-BAR setup state (SHORT; LONG mirrors):
  sl1 = most recent trigger_tf swing low with anchor_t > S.range_low_bar.t, detected_at <= b.t and not broken
        (trigger_swing_rule 'after_range_extreme', default; variant 'after_counter_bos' additionally requires detected_at > S.counter_bos_time)
  trig_bos  = sl1 exists and b.close < sl1.price  -> set sl1.broken (an EVENT that fires once per swing)
  K1 = bullish trigger_tf stack per ifvg with t0 = S.range_low_bar.t, using gaps eligible for b
  trig_ifvg = K1 exists and b.close < K1.floor   (fires once per stack)
  if neither fires: continue. If no sl1 exists, only trig_ifvg can fire.
  If b also prints a new range extreme: proceed if allow_trigger_on_new_extreme (default true), with stop = retrace_high + buffer; otherwise the NEW LEG reset applies.
  GATES at T = b.close_time, in this order (the first failure is logged):
    time: T < entry_start -> PRE_WINDOW_TRIGGER, stay ARMED | T >= cutoff or NO_TRADE day or DONE -> cancel | news block -> NEWS_WAIT, stay ARMED
    bias (daily_bias) -> BIAS_WAIT, stay ARMED
    index_alignment -> UNALIGNED, stay ARMED
    entry_premium_check (equilibrium) -> PREMIUM, stay ARMED
    stop gates (stop_loss) -> STOP_GATE, cancel | TP1 exists (take_profit) -> NO_TARGET, cancel | cost_R and contracts >= 1 (risk) -> COST / SIZE, cancel
  A 'fresh' trigger is a trigger event whose T is later than the moment the blocking condition cleared.
  ENTER: SIGNAL at T -> backtest: PENDING order filled at the next 1m open +/- slippage (backtest_execution); live: market order at the trigger close inside a bracket (live_execution).
  On entry: trades_today += 1; cancel every other setup on both indexes.
Same-T ties: iterate setups sorted by (created_at, index ES<NQ, dir, first level price_ticks), then pick in this order: with-bias direction, then the index chosen by smt_mode select_leading/select_lagging, then larger R(TP1), then earlier created_at, then ES.
entry_type '5m_close' (variant): skip the 1m trigger and enter at the close of the first confirm_tf bar closing in trade direction after zone_touched.

parameters.name: entry_type
parameters.range: tjr_1m | 5m_close | limit_fvg_edge | limit_ce (the last two are third-party)
parameters.why: 'liquidity sweep, 5-minute break of structure, one-minute break of structure to the upside and then one-minute break of structure to the downside - we're entering right there'.

parameters.name: trigger_swing_rule
parameters.why: His moving reference ('This is the low that we're looking at. Nope.') is the most recent 1m higher low of the retrace. The stricter variant ignores lows formed before the counter-BOS.

parameters.name: allow_trigger_on_new_extreme
parameters.why: Without it, a strong bar that breaks the retrace low and the range low together is reset to a new leg and never enters.

components.discretionary_notes: The event semantics, gate order and tie-breaks are ours. In a third-party test on SPY/QQQ 2016-2026, the 1m trigger carried a real gross signal and the same logic on 5m did not, so keep the trigger at 1m resolution. Third-party summary, not a TJR source: https://coconote.app/notes/525378ef-b881-47c2-9bd9-c3647adddb8e

components.name: index_alignment
components.description: Veto: no entry unless the other index agrees in 5m (confirm_tf) order flow, where order flow is updated by BOS and IFVG events.
components.algorithm:
At trigger time T for setup S on index X in direction d: Y = the other index, tf = S.ladder.confirm_tf.
  require orderflow[Y][tf] == d (BOS or stack-level IFVG, so an IFVG-confirmed index counts as aligned)
  X's own condition (align_self): 'setup_state' (default: S being ARMED already encodes X's order flow) | 'orderflow' (require orderflow[X][tf] == d)
  if Y has no data at T: not aligned (never compare a symbol with itself)
If not aligned: do not enter. Keep S ARMED and require a fresh trigger after alignment appears ('they can still get aligned later').
Day-level deadline: see schedule.alignment_deadline.
Reconciliation with SMT: divergence is allowed at the sweep; agreement is required at entry.

parameters.name: require_index_alignment
parameters.why: 'If ES is bullish on the five minute and NASDAQ is bearish, I don't want to take the trade'. Third-party tests found it hurt ES/SPY results; keep it for fidelity and test it off.

parameters.name: align_self
parameters.why: A BOS-only trend would leave an IFVG-confirmed index on the old trend and block his own first 2026 example, in which both indexes inverted a 5m gap with no BOS.

components.discretionary_notes: Video 089 says 'it doesn't matter what index', and the gate is absent in some strategy videos. A 5m retrace on Y can print a minor bullish BOS and temporarily block alignment; log UNALIGNED reasons to measure this.

components.name: stop_loss
components.description: Structural stop beyond the retrace swing (the 'second high/low') plus an instrument-scaled buffer, with gates for tiny or huge stops.
components.algorithm:
buffer_ticks = max(stop_buffer_ticks, ceil(stop_buffer_pct*price/tick)).
SHORT: stop = S.retrace_high + buffer_ticks ('stop above the second high'); LONG: stop = S.retrace_low - buffer_ticks.
stop_mode 'sweep_extreme' (2023): stop = S.sweep_extreme +- buffer. 'tiered' (video 096): the sweep extreme if it lies within max_stop, else the high/low inside the zone, else beyond the zone.
risk_ticks = |trigger_close - stop|, computed at the trigger close (known at decision time) and rechecked at the fill (backtest_execution FILL_GATE).
GATES: risk < min_stop_pct*price -> cancel (STOP_GATE); risk > max_stop_pct*price -> cancel (STOP_GATE). The wide-stop 0.5x size multiplier lives ONLY in risk.mult.
Resting stop-market order. It is never widened or removed; the only move is to break-even after TP1 (trade_management). Fill mechanics: backtest_execution.

parameters.name: stop_mode
parameters.why: 2026: 'stop above the second high'. 2023 Boot Camp: 'I almost always put my stop above the liquidity sweep'. Video 096 describes the tiered order.

parameters.name: stop_buffer_ticks
parameters.why: His buffer: 'at least 0.5 points ... or your spread' (= 2 ES ticks). The spread wording suggests a CFD origin.

parameters.name: stop_buffer_pct
parameters.why: Our assumption. It scales the buffer to NQ (about 6-7 ticks at 23,000) while ES stays at 2 ticks around 6,500.

parameters.name: min_stop_pct
parameters.why: Our assumption: below about 0.04% of price, costs exceed about 0.3R.

parameters.name: wide_stop_pct
parameters.why: His ES stops are 16-35 ticks (about 0.06-0.15% of price). Beyond this, risk.mult halves size ('if the stop is drastically larger than usual, cut the contract size in half').

parameters.name: max_stop_pct
parameters.why: Our assumption: skip trades with stops more than 2x his typical maximum.

components.discretionary_notes: He reads the 'second high' by eye; the highest high of the retrace leg since the latest range extreme is our mechanical proxy. The stop choice changes stop size by about 2x and therefore cost drag and win rate.

components.name: take_profit
components.description: Targets at opposing unswept draws on liquidity, both external (highs/lows) and internal (imbalances), not R multiples. TP1 >= 1R by default.
components.algorithm:
At signal time (SHORT; LONG mirrors), candidates strictly below the trigger close:
  external: usable alive key levels of the traded index with side LOW; alive two-candle swing lows of trading day D on S.ladder.tp_ref_tf; the SMT completion low (if SMT was detected)
  internal (if tp_include_internal): the near edge (upper boundary) of FVGs that are eligible, untouched and lie entirely below the trigger close, on tp_ref_tf and higher (15m/1H/4H); NDOG/NWOG near edges if include_opening_gaps; 1H/4H EQ of the current HTF swing range if 'EQ' in tp_internal_kinds
  drop candidates within 1 tick of the trigger close; dedupe by price_ticks; sort by distance ascending, then tf_rank descending, then cluster strength descending
  R(p) = (trigger_close - p) / risk_ticks
  TP1 = first p with R(p) >= tp1_min_R
  TP2 = next p with R(p) >= R(TP1) + tp_min_gap_R; TP3 likewise; at most max_targets
  if TP1 is None: cancel (NO_TARGET) if fallback_R is None ('no draw, no trade'), else TP1 = trigger_close - fallback_R*risk_ticks
Log each target's kind (external/internal/fallback) and which ones were hit. Resting limit orders; fill rules in backtest_execution.

parameters.name: tp1_min_R
parameters.range: 0-1.5 (0 = the nearest opposing draw whatever its R)
parameters.why: 'Most of the time my first take profit is going to be minimum one to one' is a preference. The step301 extraction finds 'no minimum-R rule': he reports R afterwards and accepts 1:1 when the stop is wide.

parameters.name: tp_ref_tf
parameters.why: Boot Camp: TP1 = the first draw on the timeframe one above execution.

parameters.name: tp_include_internal
parameters.why: 2026-06-05 names 'this big gap that we could get filled' as a target, and 2026-01-05 frames targets as external (highs/lows) vs internal (imbalances). false = external-only draft behaviour; test both.

parameters.name: tp_internal_kinds
parameters.why: FVG targets are directly attested. HTF EQ as a target is our extension.

parameters.name: max_targets
parameters.why: He sets 3-4 (up to 5) targets.

parameters.name: tp_min_gap_R
parameters.why: Our assumption, to avoid near-duplicate targets.

parameters.name: fallback_R
parameters.why: TJR targets levels only; fixed-R fallbacks are third-party.

parameters.name: tp_fill_through_ticks
parameters.why: Touch fills overstate results (third-party execution test).

components.discretionary_notes: He picks draws by eye; nearest-first ranking with tf_rank and cluster tie-breaks is ours. Third-party tests found that level-to-level targets give about 35-45% WR and that smaller fixed targets often did better; report both.

components.name: trade_management
components.description: Partial exits, the break-even move and progress/time exits, with no discretionary overrides.
components.algorithm:
q = contracts. q1 = ceil(q*tp1_close_frac); if q1 == q, exit in one piece at TP1. q2 = ceil((q - q1)*tp2_close_frac_of_remaining); q3 = q - q1 - q2.
TP1 fill: close q1; move the stop to entry -+ be_offset_ticks (active from the bar AFTER the TP1 fill).
TP2 fill: close q2; the stop stays at break-even. If TP3 is missing, q3 also closes at TP2.
If TP2 is missing: the remainder exits only via BE, stall_exit, max_hold, flat_time or pre-event flatten (no target).
Runner q3: exits at TP3, the BE stop, stall_exit, max_hold, flat_time or pre-event flatten.
STALL_EXIT: close the remainder if no new favourable extreme has printed for stall_minutes; max_hold_minutes is the backstop. Time exits fill at the open of the first bar at/after the deadline.
Never widen, remove or re-widen the stop; never add; no 'let it run' override (skipping this ladder preceded his largest losses).
After the position is flat: if trades_today == max_trades_per_day -> day DONE. Second-trade variant (max_trades_per_day = 2): a second setup may only come from a NEW sweep created after the first trade reached BE or closed in profit; never after a stop-out; both trades at 0.5x risk.
Report the distribution of q and the share of trades with a real runner (with 1-3 contracts q3 is often 0).

parameters.name: tp1_close_frac
parameters.why: Our choice, anchored on one 2023 quote (Boot Camp Day 54: 'After take profit one got hit I took off 50 of the position, my stop's at break even'). 2026-06-05 says only 'I took my first profit and then I moved my stop loss to break even'.

parameters.name: tp2_close_frac_of_remaining
parameters.why: Boot Camp 2.0: 50% of the remainder (25% of the original) at TP2. Our choice otherwise.

parameters.name: be_offset_ticks
parameters.why: 'Slightly beyond entry to cover fees'. Break-even after TP1 is well attested, including in 2026.

parameters.name: stall_minutes
parameters.why: His stated reason for manual exits is lack of progress ('price has been consolidating for literally 2 hours, 2 and 1/2 hours now, so I'm done', 2023-07-17). The threshold is ours.

components.discretionary_notes: The 50%/25% split is attested only once (2023). Other recaps say only 'take partial profits'. The 'SMC by TJRTrades' e-book (scribd/studylib) that also states the split has unverifiable provenance and may be leaked paid material, so it is not used as a source. The one-trade/day limit is his 2023 beginner recommendation; his 2025 live sessions run 2-4 trades.

components.name: risk
components.description: Position sizing, cost gate, de-risk tiers, trade limits and live kill switches.
components.algorithm:
SIZING: sizing_mode 'calculated' (default; our safety choice / his older student rule): base_risk = equity_at_session_start * risk_pct. sizing_mode 'fixed_contracts' (his 2026-01-16 practice): a fixed contract count sized so a ~35-tick worst-case stop stays within 1-3% ('sweet spot'; he tolerates 3-4%).
mult = 0.5 if any(news_halve_day, day_before_us_holiday, risk_ticks > wide_stop_pct*price, day_after_big_win (previous day >= big_win_R), second_trade, chop 'halve', orange 'halve', low_volume_day if enabled) else 1.0. Tiers do not compound; the 2x 'confident' tier is never used.
risk_dollars = base_risk * mult
per_contract = risk_ticks*tick_value + commission_rt + (slippage_ticks + stop_slippage_ticks)*tick_value
contracts = min(floor(risk_dollars / per_contract), max_contracts)
if contracts == 0 and allow_micros: switch to MES/MNQ with their own tick value and fee and recompute; still 0 -> cancel (SIZE)
cost_R = (commission_rt + (slippage_ticks + stop_slippage_ticks)*tick_value) / (risk_ticks*tick_value); cancel (COST) if cost_R > max_cost_R
max_trades_per_day = 1 (his beginner recommendation). 2 = second-trade variant (trade_management).
weekly strict_mode: OFF by default (2023 Boot Camp Day 41, contradicted 2026-06-05). If enabled: after 2 consecutive losing weeks the continuation zone must be FVG AND EQ, until a winning week.
LIVE KILL SWITCHES (ours): a broker-side daily loss limit of daily_loss_limit_mult x planned risk auto-flattens and disables the bot for the day. Rolling breaker: sum of R over the last 10 trades <= -4R, or live stats outside the backtest's 95% band -> switch to paper pending human review. derisk_after_loss (off): 0.5x after a losing week until a winning day.
Funded / prop accounts: see prop_rules.

parameters.name: risk_pct
parameters.why: Our safety default (his older student rule). On 2026-01-16 he says 'I used to do the whole thing of like calculate 1% ... but I moved away ... I'm going to risk this amount of contracts per trade', and calls 1-3% per trade the 'sweet spot'.

parameters.name: sizing_mode
parameters.why: fixed_contracts is his 2026 practice; calculated is safer for a bot and for small accounts.

parameters.name: derisk_mult
parameters.why: His de-risk tier is 0.5x (news, bank holiday, chop, wide stop).

parameters.name: big_win_R
parameters.why: Our threshold for 'I'll purposely de-risk the following day after a really big day'.

parameters.name: max_trades_per_day
parameters.why: His beginner recommendation (Boot Camp Day 29, 2023): 'I recommend one trade a day ... sometimes I'll take two'. Video 068 (2025) says 'one or two trades in a day', and Boot Camp 2.0 has a 'Second Trade' lesson.

parameters.name: commission_rt
parameters.default: ES/NQ 4.50 USD, MES/MNQ 1.25 USD per round trip (commission + exchange + NFA)
parameters.why: Our assumption. Slippage is charged in the fills only, never a second time here.

parameters.name: max_cost_R
parameters.why: Our assumption. Micros cost roughly 2-4x more in R.

parameters.name: max_contracts
parameters.why: Clamp for prop accounts and liquidity.

parameters.name: allow_micros
parameters.why: Small accounts cannot size ES/NQ at 1% on 16-35 tick stops.

parameters.name: weekly_strict_mode
parameters.why: 2023 Boot Camp Day 41 rule. Contradicted on 2026-06-05: 'I've had two losing weeks in a row ... does that mean I need to change anything? No.'

parameters.name: daily_loss_limit_mult
parameters.why: Our live safety rule; gaps, halts and disconnects can exceed one trade's planned risk.

components.discretionary_notes: Whether 1-3% is per trade or per day conflicts (2023: per day; 2026: per trade), and 'drastically larger' stop has no number. His live behaviour contradicts these rules: full-port size, 2x size, removed stops, and a -$151,780 day on 2025-11-20 after which he said 'I need to size down'. The bot follows the taught rules, not the live behaviour. Kill-switch numbers are ours.

components.name: prop_rules
components.description: Optional funded-account module: drawdown type, contract cap, consistency rule and minimum days.
components.algorithm:
Inputs: dd_type (intraday_trailing | eod_trailing | static), max_dd, max_contracts, consistency_pct, min_days, firm daily_loss_limit.
Track the high-water mark (intraday or end-of-day per dd_type) and remaining_buffer = max_dd - (HWM - equity); static: equity - (start_equity - max_dd).
risk_dollars = min(risk_pct*equity, buffer_frac*remaining_buffer, 0.5*daily_loss_limit).
Consistency guard: if today's realised P&L plus TP1 profit would exceed consistency_pct of total profit -> exit in one piece at TP1; skip the day if it is already exceeded.
Stop trading when remaining_buffer < 1R at minimum size. Clamp contracts to max_contracts. Count trading days toward min_days.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.why: Only for funded accounts.

parameters.name: buffer_frac
parameters.why: Our assumption.

parameters.name: daily_risk_cap
parameters.why: Carried over from the draft's funded-account rule.

components.discretionary_notes: His funded-accounts lesson lists trailing vs static drawdown, contract caps and consistency rules (e.g. Alpha Futures 100K: $3,500 trailing, max 10 contracts, 50% consistency; Tradeify Lightning: 20%). That content is sponsored (discount codes TJR40/TJR), a conflict of interest. In Oct 2025 (video 109) he said 'I currently do not trade on fundeds'.

components.name: filters
components.description: Calendar, news, chop and discipline gates.
components.algorithm:
CALENDAR: USD events with impact (red / orange / holiday). Backtests use an archived, dated snapshot (impact labels get revised). Live, the calendar is fetched every morning before 08:30. All times are normalised to America/New_York (Forex Factory exports use the user's configured timezone). If the fetch or parse fails -> NO_TRADE_DAY (fail closed).
EXCHANGE CALENDAR: full holiday = no session; early close -> NO_TRADE_DAY (ours); day before a US bank holiday -> risk 0.5x.
NEWS (news_mode 'tiered', default):
  FOMC decision day -> NO_TRADE_DAY (he still skipped FOMC days in Oct 2025)
  CPI/Core CPI or Non-Farm Payrolls day -> NO_TRADE_DAY (labelled 2023 Boot Camp rule; variant 'halve')
  PPI and every other red USD event at time e:
    e < 09:30: at e + post_release_wait compute spike = max 5m range in [e, e+wait) / median 5m range of that clock window over the prior 20 trading days. spike > news_spike_mult -> NO_TRADE_DAY, else risk 0.5x ('I'm just going to cut my contract size in half', 2026-01-16)
    09:30 <= e < cutoff: news block, no entries in [e - 2 min, e + post_release_wait); at e + wait apply the spike test (NO_TRADE_DAY or 0.5x). If e + wait >= cutoff, no entries today ('I will not trade until 10 a.m. hits ... until like 10:30')
  orange USD event (orange_mode 'wait', default): no entries in [e - 2 min, e + post_release_wait); variant 'halve'
  fed_speech_skip (default false; 2023-only remark): NO_TRADE_DAY on a Fed Chair speech today or yesterday
  weekly density (off): if red_events_this_week >= 4 -> cap at 2 trades/week
EVENTS WHILE IN A POSITION (ours): at entry, look up red USD events in (entry, min(entry + max_hold, flat_time)). pre_event_action 'flatten' (default) closes the position 2 min before the release -> NEWS_EXIT; variants 'move_to_BE', 'cap_hold'.
CHOP PROXY (ours; chop_mode 'log' default | 'block' | 'halve'): per index, count 5m orderflow flips in [08:30, T). The index is CHOP if flips >= chop_flip_max, OR (from 09:50) the 5m high-low range of [09:30, T) < chop_range_frac x its 20-day median at the same clock time. 'block' = no new setups on a CHOP index; 'halve' = 0.5x.
LOW VOLUME (off): at entry time T, the volume of [09:30, T) is below the 20th percentile of the same window over the prior 20 days and there is no red/orange event today -> 0.5x.
DISCIPLINE: no entry after a stop-out the same day; no averaging; no day-of-week filter (none found in TJR material; the Mon-Thu gating in the corpus belongs to a different trader). A day without a valid setup is a normal outcome ('the strategy tells you what trades not to take').

parameters.why: Boot Camp 2023: 'CPI PPI FOMC and NFP those four ... I do not trade whatsoever' (framed as beginner advice). The 2026-01-16 risk lesson halves size on a PPI day. 2025 sessions trade around releases but skip FOMC days. A third-party replay found the FOMC gate blocked a day he traded and won (2024-03-20).

parameters.name: orange_mode

parameters.name: fed_speech_skip
parameters.why: One 2023 remark; not restated since.

parameters.name: pre_event_action
parameters.why: Our rule, following his 'wait until the news comes out' logic for positions still open after the cutoff (14:00 FOMC minutes, Fed speakers).

parameters.name: chop_mode
parameters.why: Day 44 rule: 'break of structure up, sweep, break of structure, sweep, endless up and down = price garbage, no trade'. The proxy is ours, so it only logs until its marginal effect is measured.

parameters.why: Our assumption.
