components.name: backtest_execution
components.description: Order and position state machine for bar-based backtests: pending fills, gaps, intrabar ambiguity, partials and costs.
components.algorithm:
STATES: SIGNAL -> PENDING -> FILLED -> PARTIAL_TP1 -> BE -> CLOSED. Terminal cancels: GAP_SKIP, FILL_GATE.
(a) A signal at trigger close T creates a PENDING market order that fills at the open of the next 1m bar, with slippage_ticks against us.
(b) If the fill is at/beyond the stop or at/beyond TP1 -> cancel with GAP_SKIP.
(c) Recheck at the fill: risk_fill = |fill - stop|. If R_fill(TP1) < tp1_min_R - tp_recheck_tol -> cancel with FILL_GATE. Log R at the trigger and at the fill. Size stays as computed at the trigger.
(d) The fill bar is evaluated fully with its high/low.
(e) Any bar whose range contains the current stop: by intrabar_priority (default stop_first) the stop takes the whole remaining position, even if a TP is also inside the bar.
(f) Stop fills at the worse of the stop and bar.open (gap), plus stop_slippage_ticks. TP limits fill only if price trades through by tp_fill_through_ticks, and fill at the limit price (no gap price improvement).
(g) Several TPs may fill in one bar if the bar does not contain the current stop. The BE stop becomes active from the bar AFTER the TP1 fill.
(h) Time exits (stall, max_hold, flat_time, pre-event flatten) fill at the open of the first bar with t >= deadline.
P&L: fills already include slippage; the deducted cost is commission + fees only (per instrument). Slippage is never charged twice.
AMBIGUITY REPORT: share of trades touching a bar that contains both the stop and a TP. Re-resolve those bars with 1s/tick data or run a stop_first vs target_first sensitivity.

parameters.name: slippage_ticks
parameters.why: Our assumption for market fills.

parameters.name: stop_slippage_ticks
parameters.why: Our assumption.

parameters.name: intrabar_priority
parameters.why: Conservative resolution when stop and target sit inside the same 1m bar; common with 16-35 tick stops on 1m NQ.

parameters.name: tp_recheck_tol
parameters.why: Our assumption; the decision uses the trigger close, the fill uses the next open.

components.discretionary_notes: He trades by hand with market orders and brackets. These rules only make bar-based simulation deterministic and conservative.

components.name: daily_orchestration
components.description: Per-day and per-bar control loop tying all components together, with deterministic ordering.
components.algorithm:
for each trading day D (exchange calendar):
  data checks (label convention, missing minutes, roll, ES/NQ alignment) -> SKIP_DATA
  cal = filters.calendar(D); if NO_TRADE: journal the reason; continue
  warm up state from D - warmup_days on the contract traded on D
  08:30: levels[X] = key_levels(X, D) for X in (ES, NQ); setups = []; trades_today = 0; DONE = False
  for each 1m close T in [08:30, flat_time]:
    1. update the 1m bar, then every tf whose bar closed at T: swings, BOS, FVG lifecycle (touched/inverted/expired), stack IFVG events, orderflow
    2. if T == 09:25 or a 1H bar closed: bias, ladder = daily_bias(T) (new setups only; existing setups keep S.ladder)
    3. SMT evaluations whose t_eval == T
    4. if not DONE and trades_today < max_trades_per_day and T < cutoff:
         iterate setups sorted by (created_at, index ES<NQ, dir, first level price_ticks):
         a. ARMED setups: entry trigger check on the pre-bar state -> collect trigger events
         b. CONFIRMED/ARMED setups: cancel checks, new-leg update, zone / counter-BOS updates (continuation)
         c. liquidity_sweep: update alive flags, create/extend setups (new ids)
         d. if a confirm_tf bar of a setup's ladder closed: confirmation for SWEPT setups; expire stale ones
         e. triggers passing all gates -> tie-break -> SIGNAL one -> trades_today += 1 -> cancel all other setups
    5. at the first T >= alignment_deadline: schedule.alignment_deadline check (may set DONE)
    6. T >= cutoff: cancel un-entered setups
    7. backtest_execution / trade_management on the open position (live: live_execution)
  journal every setup's terminal state: EXPIRED_NO_REACTION, CANCELLED_INVALIDATION, NO_RETRACE, PRE_WINDOW_TRIGGER, UNALIGNED, BIAS_WAIT, PREMIUM, NEWS_WAIT, STOP_GATE, NO_TARGET, COST, SIZE, CUTOFF, GAP_SKIP, FILL_GATE, ENTERED, plus the day's result.

parameters.name: setup_states
parameters.why: TJR's 'potential to fill orders, confirmation, continuation, exit where orders are liquidated'.

components.discretionary_notes: He says he does not trade a rigid step list ('instead of waiting for this confirmation, I wait for another confirmation'). The state machine is our codification of his five-step summary.

components.name: journal
components.description: Per-setup and per-day journal rows for review, agreement scoring against his recaps, and debugging.
components.algorithm:
Per setup, one row: id, index, dir, ladder, bias and its inputs (trend per tf, HTF-gap flip, draws up/down), phase, swept levels (types, prices, cluster strength), sweep_time, smt flag, confirm_kind/time, EQ, zone kind, arm_time, trigger kind/time, every gate value and the first failing gate, trigger close, fill, stop, TPs (external/internal/fallback), R at trigger and at fill, cost_R, contracts and instrument, exit reasons (TP1/TP2/TP3/BE/STOP/STALL_EXIT/MAX_HOLD/FLAT/NEWS_EXIT/GAP_SKIP/FILL_GATE), realised R, plan_followed (manual overrides flagged), and a PNG snapshot of ES and NQ 5m/1m.
Per day, one row: calendar events, news decisions, chop state, alignment-deadline result, no-trade reason codes.
Export as CSV importable into a journaling tool.

parameters.name: snapshot_png
parameters.why: His journaling lesson requires a screenshot per trade.

components.discretionary_notes: Boot Camp Day 46 and rule 2 of his '6 Rules' ask for bias, confluences, entry/SL/TP, R, whether the plan was followed, and a screenshot. The field list is ours.

components.name: backtest_hygiene
components.description: Validation, determinism tests, metric definitions and data rules that third-party TJR/ICT replications showed are necessary.
components.algorithm:
1. Truncation test: re-decide every entry with all later bars deleted; decisions must be identical. Poisoned-future test: replace all bars after T with NaN or extreme values and assert identical decisions at T.
2. Unit tests: IFVG on the bar that inverts the gap (fvg); DST 4H closes include 10:00 ET every day; no swing/FVG spans a contract change; open-time bar labels (08:30 spike); a warm-up-doubled convergence test.
3. Never use centred-window pivots or shift(-1) FVG code (e.g. the smartmoneyconcepts library); one report showed PF inflated from 1.82 to 7.32.
4. Fills and costs per backtest_execution. Report costs in R per trade, not as % of notional.
5. Data: CME 1m ES/NQ futures including overnight, per contract, >= 2 years, licensed (Databento/IBKR). Cross-check with a second vendor. Avoid yfinance (60-day cap) and IEX-only equity feeds (wicks under-reported, which swung results by about 0.2R).
6. Metrics: R_trade = net_pnl / (initial_risk_ticks*tick_value*q). Win = net > 0 after costs; scratch = |R| < 0.1. Report win rate three ways (scratch as win, scratch as non-win, BE as loss, since he says 'sometimes break even trades end up being a loss'), both per trade and per day. Report realised R after partials next to R-to-TP1, and the share of ambiguous bars.
7. Golden test days: hand-label the dated examples in his public 2026 videos (e.g. the ES/NQ examples in 'My UPDATED Day Trading Strategy (2026)') with the expected sweep time, confirm kind, arm time, trigger time, stop and TP1, and keep them as regression tests. Agreement with his recaps and profitability are separate metrics.
8. Validation: chronological train/validation/sealed test, walk-forward, a penalty for every tested variant (multiple testing), a TJR-faithful configuration reported separately from any optimised one, then >= 3 months of paper trading.
9. Sanity: WR far above 64% or RR far above 1.4 -> suspect lookahead. Trading most days -> a stand-down gate was dropped. Median stop far above 0.15% of price -> swing or stop code drifted.

parameters.name: min_history_years
parameters.why: 70-day samples 'prove nothing' (third-party).

components.name: live_execution
components.description: Live/paper execution layer: brackets, reconciliation, clock, bar-builder parity and paper-first gating.
components.algorithm:
Default mode = paper/sim. Live trading requires an explicit flag, set only after >= 3 months of paper trading with stats inside the backtest band.
Orders: entry + stop-market + TP limits are submitted as a server-side OCO bracket with idempotent client order IDs. The stop is never modified except for the BE move.
On start and on reconnect: reconcile broker positions and orders against internal state before any new decision. On a mismatch: flatten, disable for the day, notify.
Clock: NTP-synced. Decisions run at the 1m close; log decision and order latency.
Live bar builder: build 1m bars from ticks with the same boundaries as the backtest vendor (open-time labels, 18:00 ET wall-clock higher-TF bins). Run a daily parity check of live vs vendor OHLC and flag deviations.
Market state: if the market is halted or limit-locked, freeze new entries and flag open positions. Risk kill switches per risk (broker-side daily loss limit, rolling breaker).
The real-time CME data licence and any broker or regulatory obligations are the user's responsibility. Signals are for the user only.

parameters.name: mode

backtest_expectations: Calibration target (TJR self-report, unaudited and publicly disputed): Jan-Jun 2026 daily win rate 64.29%. Reward:risk figures conflict: 1:1.23-1:1.33 (transcript ambiguous); about 1.375 implied by his quoted average win of ~$22,000 against an average loss of ~$16,000; and older recaps claim roughly '1 to 2 point something' realised after partials. He says break-even trades 'sometimes' count as losses in his stats. Numbers clearly better than these indicate a lookahead bug, not success.

Frequency: a faithful build (10:30 cutoff, ES/NQ alignment) traded about 2-4 times a month in third-party replays (2.2-3.1/month, run with a hard bias filter). The default 'lean' bias here is looser, so expect somewhat more trades. Loosening bias and removing the cutoff raised it to ~13.5 trade days a month. The often-cited '7-15 trade days a month' is a third-party inference, not a TJR statement; the 2023 comparisons counted days across four markets (GBPUSD, GBPJPY, gold, S&P). Trading most days means a stand-down gate was dropped.

Win rate: independent mechanical replications landed between 23% and 52%. A SPY/QQQ 2026 replay gave 23% strict and 50% after spec fixes; a full year from 2025-07 to 2026-07 gave 46.3% over 244 trades. The MT5 bachelor thesis (43.6% WR, PF 1.18 backtest) ran on NVIDIA, not ES/NQ, and used a fixed ET_UTC_OffsetHours=-5 (the DST bug). Its 'forward PF 0.68' covers only 6 trades and is not evidence either way.

Costs dominate. On SPY/QQQ 2016-2026 the 1m trigger had a real gross edge (+0.065% of price per entry, t about 9.8), but net R was -0.24 at a 0.04% round trip, because the median stop is only about 0.08% of price. On ES/NQ futures expect about 0.04-0.06R cost per trade, and 2-4x that on micros. Always report cost_R.
Stop sanity: the median stop should be about 0.06-0.15% of price (ES about 16-35 ticks). Much wider means the swing or stop code drifted to fractals or to the sweep extreme.
The 1m trigger is load-bearing: collapsing it to 5m removed the gross edge in a third-party test (+0.0055% vs +0.0654% per entry).

Level-to-level targets typically give about 35-45% WR, and smaller fixed targets raise WR. Report the TJR-faithful configuration separately from any optimised one. With internal (FVG) targets enabled, expect closer TP1s and a slightly higher WR.

Third-party partition tests found that EQ/FVG continuation and daily-bias agreement did not reliably select better entries; the HTF-gap bias flip was the only bias change that improved P&L. Measure each gate's marginal effect, including require_zone_touch true vs false and bias lean vs filter.

Metric definitions: R_trade = net_pnl / (initial_risk_ticks*tick_value*q). Win = net > 0 after costs; scratch = |R| < 0.1. Report WR three ways (scratch as win, scratch as non-win, BE as loss), both per trade and per day. Report realised R after partials alongside R-to-TP1.

Report the share of trades touching an ambiguous bar (stop and TP inside one 1m bar) and the stop_first vs target_first sensitivity. With 1-3 contracts a runner (q3) often does not exist; report the distribution of q.
Agreement with his published trade recaps (day + direction) and profitability are separate metrics: one bot reached 54% agreement on 73 recap days and still lost money.

Validation: >= 2 years of per-contract 1m ES/NQ futures, a sealed hold-out, walk-forward, a penalty for every variant tested, a second data vendor, golden test days, then >= 3 months of paper trading before real money.

Core parts of his method are discretionary: which draw is 'the' draw, the exact 'second high' stop, chop detection, news-reaction size, bias overrides, trend phase and manual exits. The deterministic proxies are labelled. He himself says an automated version would not make everyone rich.

His rules changed over time: order blocks dropped (2026-02-03), leading vs lagging SMT (unresolved in 2026), 1% sizing replaced by fixed contracts, news skip vs halve, 10:30 vs 11:00 cutoff, stop at the sweep vs at the retrace swing, one vs two trades a day, zone required vs optional. The newest material is the default where it is clear; older or conflicting rules are exposed as parameters or variants.

Execution venue: there is no public evidence that he executes on CME ES/NQ futures. 2023 recap titles use CFD symbols, Boot Camp 2.0 documents AirFX on MT5, and his 2026 figures are 'before fees and swap'. On the other hand, in 2026 he talks about contracts and ES ticks. CME futures are used here as a data proxy. CFD costs (spread, swap) and 4H bar alignment differ.

His performance figures are self-reported and unaudited, and a widely viewed expose alleges some live trades were chart drawings. His live behaviour (full-port size, moved or removed stops, re-entries, a -$151,780 day on 2025-11-20) contradicts his teaching, so copying his live calls is not the same as running his rules.
Independent faithful replications did not reproduce his results and were break-even to negative after costs. Expect far fewer trades and lower win rates than he reports.

Many numbers were never given by him and are our assumptions: level lookbacks, sweep expiry, leg cap, equal-high tolerance, FVG minimum/expiry/stacking, stop buffer (incl. NQ scaling) and min/max stop, news spike threshold, chop thresholds, stall and max-hold minutes, draw radius, cost_R cap, kill-switch levels, NDOG/NWOG handling and the phase state machine.

Exchange facts (tick values, roll dates, price limits) come from general knowledge because cmegroup.com was blocked; verify them against CME contract specs. The local corpus also contained transcripts of other traders (Craig Percoco, Alex Gonzalez); these were not attributed to TJR.

Data requirements: synchronised per-contract 1m ES and NQ futures including overnight sessions, plus an archived economic calendar. SPY/QQQ lack Asia/London data, and free feeds cap history at about 60 days or under-report wicks.

Paid or private material (Whop community, Discord, Mastermind, Blueprint, leaked course files) was not and must not be used. The 'SMC by TJRTrades' e-book on scribd/studylib has unverifiable provenance and is not relied on. His prop-firm lessons are sponsored (discount codes), a conflict of interest.

This is an educational specification only, not financial advice. Futures are leveraged. Run on paper/demo first. Real-time CME data licences are the user's responsibility, and sharing live signals with other people may carry regulatory obligations.

persona_style:
Use this for recognising and classifying content only. Never put this text into a generation prompt and never imitate it. Summaries are written in a neutral third person with attribution ('In his video <title> (<date>), TJR explains ...'), plus a link and timestamp. They are never in his first person and never signed as him.

Markers that help classify his uploads:
- blunt, casual, sometimes profane speech ('freaking')
- heavy repetition and rhetorical Q&A ('Is it a liquidity sweep? No. Because it's not reacting to it.')
- numbered step frameworks (draws -> sweep -> confirmation -> continuation -> entry -> exit at opposing draws)
- 'Boom'/'Awesome' when confluences line up
- ES and NQ charts side by side
- P&L in titles, including large losses
- constant stress on simplicity, patience and filtering

Mantras that may be quoted briefly with attribution: 'higher time frames hold higher power'; 'a day out of the market is better than a day in the market'; 'stop marrying your bias'; 'our strategy is less about what trade to take and more about what trades it stops us from taking'; 'keep it simple stupid'; 'you suck, your strategy doesn't'; 'seek and destroy' (the market stopping out the obvious AM entries before the real move); 'full port' (max size, which he tells students never to use).

Content types: structured lessons (Path to Profitability, Boot Camp, Advanced Liquidity/Imbalance Concepts), live-trade recaps, lifestyle vlogs, promos/trailers and crypto guides. Only lessons and recaps carry rule information, and newer videos override older ones ('the boot camp is dated ... I do not trade the same way').
